subject: Latency stress scenarios & qualification — next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@clearline.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Latency stress scenarios & qualification — next steps

Samantha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size the pilot and calibrate the cost/perf levers.

Recap (what you asked):
- 99th pctl target: 120ms for single-turn text generation (prompt ~200 tokens).
- Streaming use case: live transcription + realtime suggestions with <200ms token emission latency requirement.
- Peak concurrency: expected bursts to 450 concurrent request streams during campaign windows, steady-state ~60 concurrent.
- Throughput: typical qps ~55, peak qps in bursts ~380.

Checks we need from your side:
1) Confirmation of exact 99th percentile SLA target (is 120ms hard or negotiable to 150ms with fallbacks?).
2) Representative payloads: sample prompts and expected output lengths (attach a small CSV or text file).
3) Peak schedule: any known daily/hourly windows where bursts will happen (timezone & cron).

Redwood proposed qualification plan (high level):
- Short smoke run in our hosted sandbox: 5k tokens/session, run through model variants to chart latency curves.
- Streaming stress test using continuous-batching disabled and enabled to measure token emission latency vs throughput.
- Cost levers to test: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, int8 quantized variants, and a fallback model (smaller model for heavy bursts).

Immediate next steps:
- If you can drop the sample payloads and a 2-week peak schedule into the Drive link, we’ll prepare a tailored test matrix.
- I’ll loop in Karthik for the quantization options and Ben for streaming-runbook decisions.

Attachments: clearline_latency_samples.csv (placeholder), mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (MVP scope & milestones).

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Latency stress scenarios & qualification — next steps

Thanks Marcus — this is great. Quick answers inline.

> 99th pctl target: 120ms for single-turn text generation (prompt ~200 tokens).
We can be flexible on an initial pilot. 120ms is our goal for GA; for pilot, 150ms is acceptable as long as degradation is clearly characterized and there27s a plan to reach 120ms by production.

> Streaming use case: live transcription + realtime suggestions with <200ms token emission latency requirement.
This is firm for the suggestion experience; transcription-only flows can tolerate up to 400ms.

Payloads: I uploaded five representative prompts + expected responses to the Drive folder (file: clearline_latency_samples.csv). The CSV also contains a boolean column indicating streaming vs non-streaming.

Peak schedule: main bursts Monday 09:00-11:00 PST and 18:00-19:00 PST; weekend campaigns are sporadic. Peak length ~90 minutes.

Two clarifying asks for Redwood team:
- Can you quantify expected cost delta for enabling continuous batching vs disabling it for streaming?
- For the fallback model strategy, what’s the expected quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE or a short eval) when falling back to an int8 quantized model?

We27d like an initial test run next week if that works. Please send an action plan and who to expect on the technical session.

—Samantha
Head of Product Engineering
Clearline AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Cho <samantha@clearline.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency stress scenarios & qualification — next steps

Marcus / Ben — a couple of technical notes to include in the test matrix.

1) Quantization profiles: we should test three profiles across the same workload: fp16 (baseline), int8 dynamic, and int8 static with KV-cache-friendly layout. Track generation latency, peak GPU memory, and a small automated quality delta (we can run a BLEU-style token overlap & perplexity on the sample set).

2) Continuous batching: for streaming flows, continuous batching reduces GPU overhead but adds queuing latency per-token. I suggest:
- Streaming A: continuous batching ON, 50ms max batching window
- Streaming B: continuous batching OFF (no batching), baseline per-token latency measured
Collect token emission latency distributions and 95/99/100p values.

3) Caching: prefix caching may help if prompts have substantial shared prefixes; add an experiment with and without prefix caching enabled.

4) Fallback routing: define a policy that triggers fallback when measured 95th pctl token emission latency exceeds 180ms for >30s. Fallback route: smaller quantized variant with shorter response length cap.

I27ll prepare the test matrix and a small script to synthesize concurrency bursts to match their 450-concurrent peak.

Karthik
Director, Applied ML
Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks for the quick responses. Plan for next week:

- Monday 11/09 10:00 PST: 60-min technical session (Redwood + Clearline ops & eng). Agenda: 1) sample data walkthrough, 2) confirm streaming vs non-streaming labels, 3) finalize test matrix. (Calendar invite to follow.)
- Tuesday 11/10 09:00 PST: sandbox smoke run (Redwood runs automated matrix with 30-min stress burst). We27ll share results and a recommendation doc the same day.

What we27ll deliver after the smoke run:
- Latency & token emission distributions (p50/p95/p99), memory & GPU utilization charts.
- Cost delta estimates across the levers you asked about (continuous batching on/off, quantized variants, caching impact). We27ll show cost-per-100k tokens and projected monthly bill for your steady-state and burst scenarios.
- A proposed fallback policy (Karthik27s thresholds) and a short quality regression report for the int8 fallback variant.

Action items for Clearline before Monday: drop the sample CSV (done), share an ops contact for ramp coordination (ops.eng@clearline.ai is fine).

I attached the mutual action plan v1 with milestones and owners. Let us know if you want any changes before the invite.

Best,
Marcus
